correctness.rationale: In the stated saturated four-site chain, positive internal rates allow any state to be emptied at the right and rebuilt from the left. Reflection swaps c,d and reverses the signed current. A fresh exact 16-state generator solve gives the cross-difference −cd(c−d)P(c,d)/D(c,d), with all 154 coefficients of D positive and least total degree two. After c=rh,d=h, D/h² is strictly positive. All 17 ascending-h coefficient rows agree with the separate frozen arrays. The p11 and p12 factors cannot add a sign change: for r≥2 the shift of A is positive, and for 1<r≤2 the negative terms of B dominate. The remaining coefficients give exactly two sign changes. The constant and leading coefficients are positive and the exact negative witness P_r(1/r)=−2T(r)/r⁹ forces one root on either side. Descartes then gives exactly two simple roots, and the negative prefactor gives the negative–positive–negative polarity pattern. This proof uses the explicit rate rules, not their historical attribution.
residual_risks: The exact historical factor-of-two rate mapping to Sakai–Akimoto was not independently verified from the model section; the explicit generator and mathematical theorem do not depend on that mapping.
The assertion is for h>0, r>1 and full reservoir bias; it does not prove a reversal theorem at degenerate rates or lower bias.
